beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Champ, this garden is seven feet long and four feet wide. How much edging will go all the way around?

do.text: How long is the whole border?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Seven and four. Eleven feet!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Let's lay it down. Seven feet along here. Four feet around the corner.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: It stops! We haven't reached the start.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A rectangle's opposite sides match. Another seven along this side. Then four to reach the start. Perimeter means the distance all the way around.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Unpin the border at the start. Keep every piece the same length. Let's straighten one corner at a time.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven stays. Swing the next pieces out together.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Open the next corner. Then the last corner.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven, then four, then seven, then four. The end reaches twenty two feet.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So the perimeter is the whole border, laid out straight.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Fold the same pieces back. Their length never changed.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: We can add these same pieces in different groups. Bring the two sevens together.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two sevens make fourteen. Two fours make eight. Fourteen plus eight is twenty two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Or put them back in walking order: seven and four, twice. Eleven and eleven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try a rectangle nine centimeters by three centimeters. Picture the entire walk. What is its perimeter?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Nine, three, nine, three. Twenty four centimeters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A square has four equal sides. Each is six centimeters. Four sixes make twenty four centimeters around.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This rectangle has a perimeter of thirty centimeters. One side is nine. How long is the missing side?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The opposite side must be nine too. And the two unknown sides match.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Lay the thirty centimeter border straight. Move both nines together: eighteen centimeters already known.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Take away those eighteen. Thirty minus eighteen leaves twelve centimeters for both unknown sides.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Twelve is for two sides! Share it equally. Six centimeters each.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Put the sides back in order, and fold them around the rectangle.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Fold the first corner. Fold the next corner. Close the border. Nine plus six plus nine plus six is thirty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A triangle has three sides. Five, six, seven centimeters. Add every side once: eighteen centimeters around.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back at our garden, perimeter measures the border: twenty two feet of edging.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Area measures the space inside. This little square is one foot by one foot: one square foot.

do.meaning: Space covered, counted in unit squares.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven squares in each row. Four rows. Twenty eight square feet of soil surface.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Multiplying measured the inside. Adding the sides measured the border.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Can different rectangles need the same length of border? Here are five by three, and six by two, in centimeters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Their areas are fifteen and twelve square centimeters. Different amounts of space inside.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Straighten both borders. Five, three, five, three. Six, two, six, two.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Both reach sixteen! Same perimeter, different rectangles.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Whether the border bends or lies straight, we count the same length.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Perimeter is every side, once, all the way around.
